summary: Rovers on Mars is an educational Scratch animation created by elementary school students for the Abandoned But Not Forgotten challenge. Set against a Martian landscape, the project introduces NASA's Perseverance, Curiosity, and Opportunity rovers one by one—sharing each rover's launch date, whether it remains active today, and the real story behind why Opportunity's mission ended—to honor the robotic explorers that paved the way on the Red Planet.
details:
What It Does:

Rovers on Mars is an educational animation built in Scratch that pays tribute to NASA's robotic Mars explorers. Starting with an image of Mars, three famous rovers—Perseverance, Curiosity, and Opportunity—enter the screen one at a time from left to right. As each rover appears, it tells the viewer its official launch date and whether it is currently active or inactive, including the real reason why Opportunity's mission came to an end.

How It Works & How We Built It:

Our elementary school team (grades 2–4) created this project in Scratch by researching official mission facts for each rover and translating them into an animated story. We programmed sequential entrances, smooth horizontal movement across the Martian terrain, and timed dialogue bubbles so viewers can easily follow each rover's history without feeling overwhelmed by text.

Why It Matters:

Even after a spacecraft powers down, its scientific discoveries continue to help humanity. By spotlighting both active rovers (Perseverance and Curiosity) and retired pioneers (Opportunity), our project helps young students appreciate the dedication behind space exploration and ensures these robotic heroes are remembered.

Tools & Resources Used:

- Scratch (MIT) for programming sequential movement, scene timing, and dialogue

- Custom Mars landscape background and rover sprites

- Official NASA Mars Exploration Program data (launch dates, mission statuses, and historical records for Perseverance, Curiosity, and Opportunity)
